```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(openxlsx2)
library(haven)
```

# Load Genus abundance and taxonomy data

```{r prepare abundance and taxonomy data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# load microbe abundance data at genus level
microbiome_abundance_data.tb <- read_tsv("../../microbiome-data/dada2rb-genus-count.txt") %>% 
  # remove NA in subject IDs
  filter(!is.na(SEQN)) %>% 
  column_to_rownames("SEQN")

# load taxonomy and split the single taxonomy levels
microbiome_taxonomy_data.tb <- read_tsv("../../microbiome-data/dada2rb-taxonomy-annotate.txt") %>% 
  # split taxonomy into its pieces
  separate_wider_delim(cols = `Taxonomy in SILVA v123`, delim = ";", names = c("Domain", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus"), too_few = "align_start") %>% 
  column_to_rownames("Name")

# create a taxonomy subset for the wanted level
taxonomy_subset.tb <- microbiome_taxonomy_data.tb[colnames(microbiome_abundance_data.tb),]

# Many taxonomies are incomplete, wherever "NA" is present, replace the "NA"
# NB: "NA", not actual NA
na_coords <- which(taxonomy_subset.tb == "NA", arr.ind = TRUE)

# Replace those specific coordinates with the corresponding row names
taxonomy_subset.tb[na_coords] <- rownames(taxonomy_subset.tb)[na_coords[, "row"]]
```

# Prepare metadata

```{r}
metadata.list <- list()
```

## Alpha diversities (median of 10 rarefaction and measurements)

This value was already calculated by the Knight Lab and made available with 
NHANES microbiome data.

```{r}
# load alpha diversities on rarefied 10k counts
alpha_diversities <- read_tsv("../../microbiome-data/dada2rsv-alpha.txt") %>% 
  column_to_rownames("SEQN") %>% 
  # convert to numeric, R will force NA in 160 cases where "." is present
  mutate_all(.funs = as.double)

alpha_diversities <- select(alpha_diversities, contains(c("SEQN", "_10000")))

# there are multiple repetitions for each rarefaction, to 
# assess stability of the random subsampling. calculate median every 10 columns

alpha_observed_median <- alpha_diversities %>% 
  select(contains("Observed")) %>% apply(1, median)

alpha_faith_median <- alpha_diversities %>% 
  select(contains("FaPhylo")) %>% apply(1, median)

alpha_Shannon_median <- alpha_diversities %>% 
  select(contains("ShanW")) %>% apply(1, median)

metadata.list[["alpha_diversities"]] <- tibble(
  SEQN = names(alpha_observed_median),
  alpha_Observed = alpha_observed_median,
  alpha_Faith = alpha_faith_median,
  alpha_Shannon = alpha_Shannon_median
)

```

## Diet scores

  1. Healthy Eating Index 2020: total score (`HEI2020_ALL`) and its 13 components (`HEI2020_*`)
  2. NOVA food processing groups 1-4: absolute intake in kcal and grams (`novaX_kcal`, `novaX_g`) and proportion of calories and grams (`novaX_propcal`, `novaX_propg`)
     - Ultraprocessed Foods score by calories: `nova4_propcal`
     - Ultraprocessed Foods score by grams of food: `nova4_propg`

The file also includes survey design variables and weights, demographics, health covariates, and dietary recall quality flags.

MaPiDS is not yet computed (see `../../MAPiDs/` for the specification).

```{r}
metadata.list[["diet_scores"]] <- read_xlsx("../../diet-indices-from-Mukta/analytic_cleanHEI_NOVA_Mukta_2026_08_19.xlsx")
```

## NOVA subgroups

NOVA subgroups from the raw NOVA files (`../../NOVA food processing files/`), with the same four measures as the NOVA groups: `novasgX_kcal`, `novasgX_g`, `novasgX_propcal`, `novasgX_propg`. As for the NOVA groups in Mukta's file, values are averaged over the reliable recall days (`day1_ok`, `day2_ok`).

| NOVA group | Subgroups |
|------------|-----------|
| 1 (unprocessed / minimally processed) | 1 Legumes; 2 Roots and tubers; 3 Vegetables; 5 Fruit including juices; 6 Meat/poultry; 7 Fish; 8 Eggs; 9 Milk & yogurt; 10 Grains; 12 Pasta; 13 Other g1 |
| 2 (processed culinary ingredients) | 14 Table sugar; 15 Oils; 16 Animal fats; 17 Other g2 |
| 3 (processed) | 18 Cheese; 19 Ham and salted meats; 20 Plant foods in brine; 21 Other g3; 214 Salty commercial baby foods; 215 Fruit commercial baby foods |
| 4 (ultra-processed) | 22 Reconstituted meat or fish products; 23 Bread; 24 Cakes, cookies, pies, pancakes and pastries; 25 Ice cream, ice pops and frozen yogurts; 26 Desserts and other sugary products; 27 Sugared breakfast cereals; 28 Salty snacks; 29 Sweet snacks; 30 Frozen and shelf-stable plate meals; 31 Pizza; 32 Sandwiches and hamburgers on bun; 33 French fries and potato products; 34 Instant and canned soups; 36 Sauces, dressings, gravies; 37 Sugared milk drinks; 38 Soft drinks, carbonated; 39 Other sweetened beverages; 41 Other g4; 43 Instant formula |

```{r}
nova_files <- list.files("../../NOVA food processing files", pattern = "^nh(0910|1112)\\.day[12]\\.nova.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

nova_subgroups_long.df <- nova_files %>%
  map(read_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  # drop the day prefix so day 1 and day 2 columns can be stacked
  map(rename_with, .fn = ~ sub("^DR[12]T_", "", .x)) %>%
  map(select, SEQN = seqn, DAY, contains("Novasg")) %>%
  bind_rows()

# reliable recall days, as defined in Mukta's file
reliable_days.df <- metadata.list[["diet_scores"]] %>%
  select(SEQN, day1_ok, day2_ok) %>%
  pivot_longer(-SEQN, names_to = "DAY", values_to = "ok") %>%
  mutate(DAY = as.numeric(sub("day([12])_ok", "\\1", DAY))) %>%
  filter(ok)

metadata.list[["nova_subgroups"]] <- nova_subgroups_long.df %>%
  semi_join(reliable_days.df, by = c("SEQN", "DAY")) %>%
  group_by(SEQN) %>%
  summarise(across(contains("Novasg"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  # match naming of NOVA groups in Mukta's file, e.g. novasg23_kcal
  rename_with(~ .x %>%
                sub("^Abscal_Novasg([0-9]+)$", "novasg\\1_kcal", .) %>%
                sub("^Absgram_Novasg([0-9]+)$", "novasg\\1_g", .) %>%
                sub("^Propcal_Novasg([0-9]+)$", "novasg\\1_propcal", .) %>%
                sub("^Propgram_Novasg([0-9]+)$", "novasg\\1_propg", .))
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Open question for Mukta

The group 4 subgroups sum to Mukta's `nova4_kcal` (up to floating point error) for 10,232 of 10,241 participants. For the remaining 9, `nova4_kcal` is NA in Mukta's file, but the raw NOVA files have values, so the subgroup columns are filled in for them:

SEQN 52813, 57963, 58263, 63147, 64029, 64377, 64399, 66187, 70226

Ask Mukta why these were set to NA and whether the subgroups should be set to NA as well.
:::

## Other metadata - oral health

  - OHDDESTS: Oral Health - dentition status score 
  - derive number of total teeth from variables `OHX[0-9]?TC`:
    - if 1, primary (deciduous) tooth present
    - if 2, permanent tooth is present
    - if 3, implant is present
    - if 4, none of the above

```{r}
oral_health_2009 <- haven::read_xpt("../../2009-2010/OHXDEN_F.xpt") %>% mutate(NHANES_year = "2009-2010", .after = "SEQN")
oral_health_2011 <- haven::read_xpt("../../2011-2012/OHXDEN_G_exam.xpt") %>% mutate(NHANES_year = "2011-2012", .after = "SEQN")

oral_health_complete.df <- data.frame(bind_rows(oral_health_2009, oral_health_2011))
rownames(oral_health_complete.df) <- oral_health_complete.df$SEQN

teeth_count_variabes <- sprintf("OHX%.2dTC", 1:32)
tmp <- select(oral_health_complete.df, teeth_count_variabes)

number_teeth.df <- oral_health_complete.df %>% 
  mutate(
    OH_n_natural_teeth = rowSums(tmp <= 2),
    OH_n_implants = rowSums(tmp == 3),
    OH_n_no_teeth_nor_implants = rowSums(tmp == 4),
    .after = SEQN
  )

```

## Other metadata - nitric oxide exhalation

  - Nitric Oxide exhalation: 4 measurements (ENXTR1Q, ENXTR2Q, ENXTR3Q, ENXTR4Q)

```{r}
nitrate_2009 <- haven::read_xpt("../../2009-2010/ENX_F_exam.xpt") %>% mutate(NHANES_year = "2009-2010", .after = "SEQN")
nitrate_2011 <- haven::read_xpt("../../2011-2012/ENX_G_exam.xpt") %>% mutate(NHANES_year = "2011-2012", .after = "SEQN")

nitrate_exhalation.df <- bind_rows(nitrate_2009, nitrate_2011) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  transmute(
    SEQN,
    NHANES_year,
    OH_nitric_oxide_exhalation = mean(c(ENXTR1Q, ENXTR2Q, ENXTR3Q, ENXTR4Q), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```

```{r}
oral_health.df <- full_join(number_teeth.df, nitrate_exhalation.df, by = c("SEQN", "NHANES_year")) %>% 
  # remove cases of all-NA
  filter(!all(is.na(OH_nitric_oxide_exhalation), is.na(OH_n_natural_teeth), is.na(OH_n_implants), is.na(OH_n_no_teeth_nor_implants)))

metadata.list[["oral_health"]] <- oral_health.df
```

## Make complete metadata

```{r}
metadata_complete.df <- metadata.list %>% 
  lapply(mutate, SEQN = as.character(SEQN)) %>% 
  purrr::reduce(full_join, by = "SEQN") %>% 
  DataFrame()

rownames(metadata_complete.df) <- metadata_complete.df$SEQN
```

# Merge into Summarized Experiment

```{r}
# first make sure only availables samples are present and in the same order
metadata_only_microbiome.df <- metadata_complete.df[match(rownames(microbiome_abundance_data.tb), metadata_complete.df$SEQN),]

# one last filtering for full availability of microbiome and metadata
samples_intersect <- intersect(rownames(microbiome_abundance_data.tb), metadata_complete.df$SEQN)
metadata_only_microbiome.df <- metadata_complete.df[samples_intersect,]
microbiome_abundance_data.tb <- microbiome_abundance_data.tb[samples_intersect,]

NHANES_oral_microbiome.se <- SummarizedExperiment(
  assays = list("counts" = t(microbiome_abundance_data.tb)),
  rowData = DataFrame(taxonomy_subset.tb), 
  colData = DataFrame(metadata_only_microbiome.df)
)

# Keep samples with a minimum of 10k counts
NHANES_oral_microbiome.se <- NHANES_oral_microbiome.se[,colSums(assay(NHANES_oral_microbiome.se)) > 10000]
```

```{r}
save(NHANES_oral_microbiome.se, file = "../NHANES_oral_microbiome.se.rda")
```
